chapters.title: Genesis 1: The Beginning
chapters.subtitle: Creation of the Cosmos, Earth, and Life
chapters.synopsis: In the beginning, God brings forth light out of darkness, shapes the sky and the seas, commands the land to blossom, sets the sun, moon, and stars in the heavens, fills the world with living creatures, and crowns creation with humanity in His image.

panels.altText: Cosmic waters in darkness with radiant Spirit of God hovering above the deep

bubbles.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth. The earth was formless and empty, darkness was over the deep, and the Spirit of God hovered over the waters.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 1:1–2

panels.altText: Divine dawn breaking across the cosmic expanse, piercing through primeval darkness

bubbles.text: And God said, 'Let there be light,' and there was light. God saw that the light was good, and He separated the light from the darkness, calling the light 'Day' and the darkness 'Night'.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 1:3–5

bubbles.text: LET THERE BE LIGHT!
bubbles.speaker: The Almighty

panels.altText: Atmospheric sky expanse parting cosmic waters with azure twilight horizons

bubbles.text: God commanded a vast expanse to appear between the waters, parting the waters above from the waters below. God called the expanse 'Sky.'
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 1:6–8

bubbles.text: A wide space will appear between the waters!
bubbles.speaker: The Almighty

panels.altText: Verdant emerald continents emerging from azure oceans with lush plants and blooming trees

bubbles.text: The waters under the sky gathered into one place, and dry ground appeared called 'Land.' Green vegetation, seed-bearing plants, and fruit trees burst forth across the earth.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 1:9–13

bubbles.text: Let dry ground appear, and let the earth bring forth plants with seeds and fruit trees!
bubbles.speaker: The Almighty

panels.altText: Golden sun, silver moon, and swirling galaxies illuminating the celestial heavens

bubbles.text: God established lights in the expanse of the sky: the greater light to govern the day, the lesser light to govern the night, and countless stars to mark times, days, and years.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 1:14–19

panels.altText: Whales and schools of fish leaping through sapphire waves while birds soar through clouds

bubbles.text: The ocean depths surged with swimming creatures and majestic sea life, while birds of every kind took flight across the open sky. God blessed them to be fruitful and multiply.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 1:20–23

panels.altText: Magnificent lions, deer, and creatures grazing peacefully across sunny plains

bubbles.text: The earth brought forth living creatures of every kind: cattle, creeping creatures, and wild beasts roaming across valleys and hills.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 1:24–25

panels.altText: Silhouettes of man and woman standing atop a sunlit ridge looking over the magnificent creation

bubbles.text: Then God created humanity in His own image—male and female He created them—and blessed them to steward the earth. God saw everything that He had made, and it was very good.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 1:26–31

bubbles.text: Let us make human beings in our image, like ourselves.
bubbles.speaker: The Almighty

chapters.title: Genesis 2: The Garden of Eden & The First Union
chapters.subtitle: The Sabbath rest, the formation of Adam, the planting of Eden, and the creation of woman
chapters.synopsis: God blesses the seventh day as a day of sacred rest. Adam is formed from the dust of the earth and placed into the Garden of Eden to tend it. Finding no companion among the animals he names, God causes a deep sleep to fall upon him and fashions the first woman from his side, establishing the covenant of marriage.

panels.event: The Seventh Day of Rest & Blessing of the Sabbath
panels.altText: Tranquil Eden paradise valley at golden dawn, serene mountain reflections and Sabbath rest over the finished earth

bubbles.speaker: Genesis 2:1–3
bubbles.text: Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them. On the seventh day God ended His work; and He blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because in it He rested from all His work.

panels.event: The Formation of Man from the Dust of the Earth
panels.altText: Newly formed Adam waking upon rich moist soil in the morning mist as divine breath infuses him with life

bubbles.speaker: Genesis 2:7
bubbles.text: And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

panels.event: The Planting of Eden and the Four Rivers
panels.altText: The magnificent garden eastward in Eden with crystal turquoise rivers dividing into four headwaters amid ancient trees

bubbles.speaker: Genesis 2:8–10
bubbles.text: The Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden. In the midst stood the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge, nourished by a great river that parted into four heads: Pishon, Gihon, Tigris, and Euphrates.

panels.altText: Adam standing reverently beneath towering fruit canopies in the Eden sanctuary as divine commandment is given

bubbles.speaker: The Lord God
bubbles.text: “You may freely eat of every tree of the garden; but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, you shall not eat of it; for in the day that you eat thereof you shall surely die.”

bubbles.speaker: Genesis 2:15
bubbles.text: The Lord God took the man and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.

panels.event: Adam Naming the Animals (Adam visibly interacting with creatures)
panels.altText: Adam kneeling peacefully in a sunny meadow interacting with creatures brought before him to be named

bubbles.speaker: Genesis 2:18–19
bubbles.text: The Lord God said: “It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” And out of the ground God formed every beast and bird, and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them.

bubbles.speaker: Adam
bubbles.text: “Stag... Eagle... Horse... yet among all these living creatures, none is a counterpart to share my spirit.”

panels.event: The Deep Sleep of Adam & Creation of the Woman
panels.altText: Adam resting in peaceful deep slumber upon a mossy embankment while God gently fashions the woman from his side

bubbles.speaker: Genesis 2:21–22
bubbles.text: And the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and He took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh. And the rib He made into a woman, and brought her unto the man.

panels.event: Adam Meets the Woman and Joyfully Speaks
panels.altText: Adam looking upon the newly created woman with eyes of wonder and speaking with joyful love in the sunlit garden

bubbles.speaker: Adam
bubbles.text: “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh! She shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man!”

bubbles.speaker: Genesis 2:23
bubbles.text: Adam awakes and beholds the one created to walk in joyful companionship with him in Eden.

panels.event: The Covenant of Marriage & Innocent Harmony in Eden
panels.altText: The man and his wife standing together hand-in-hand in pure, innocent fellowship in the paradise garden

bubbles.speaker: Genesis 2:24–25
bubbles.text: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh. And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.

chapters.title: Genesis 3: The Fall of Humanity
chapters.subtitle: The Serpent's Deception and Expulsion from Paradise
chapters.synopsis: The serpent deceives Eve into eating the forbidden fruit of the Tree of Knowledge. Adam eats as well. Their eyes are opened to shame; God confronts them and clothes them with garments of skin before sending them forth.

panels.altText: The mysterious serpent coiled around the Tree of Knowledge, whispering softly in the shadows

bubbles.text: The serpent, more crafty than any wild animal, whispered doubt to Eve regarding God's command. Seeing the fruit pleasing to the eye and desirable for gaining wisdom, she took and ate, and gave some to her husband.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 3:1–6
The Serpent
bubbles.text: Did God really say, 'You must not eat from any tree in the garden'?

bubbles.speaker: Eve
bubbles.text: We may eat fruit from the trees, but God said of the tree in the middle, 'Do not eat it or you will die.'

panels.altText: Adam and Eve crouching in the shadows of tangled thickets under dramatic rays of divine light

bubbles.text: Hearing the sound of the Lord God walking in the garden in the cool of the day, Adam and Eve hid themselves among the trees, trembling in their nakedness.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 3:8–13

bubbles.text: Where are you, Adam?
bubbles.speaker: The Lord God
Adam
bubbles.text: I heard your sound in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid.

panels.altText: The blazing fiery sword of the Cherubim guarding the golden gates of Eden as travelers journey east

bubbles.text: The Lord God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them. To guard the way to the Tree of Life, He placed cherubim and a flaming sword flashing back and forth at the east of Eden.

chapters.title: Genesis 4: Cain and Abel
chapters.subtitle: The Two Offerings, Envy, and The First Murder
chapters.synopsis: Eve bears Cain, a tiller of soil, and Abel, a keeper of flocks. God looks with favor on Abel's offering. Overcome with jealousy, Cain slays his brother in the field and is marked by God as a wandering exile.

panels.altText: Two stone altars: one offering smoking cleanly toward heaven, the other heavy with dark smoldering ash

bubbles.text: In the course of time, Cain brought fruits of the soil as an offering, while Abel brought fat portions from some of the firstborn of his flock. The Lord looked with favor on Abel and his offering, but on Cain's He did not.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 4:1–5

panels.altText: Cain standing alone in a barren windswept field under an ominous crimson sunset

bubbles.text: Cain attacked his brother Abel in the open field. When the Lord inquired of Abel, Cain retorted defiantly. God replied: 'Your brother’s blood cries out to me from the ground!'
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 4:8–12

bubbles.text: Where is your brother Abel?
bubbles.speaker: The Lord
Cain
bubbles.text: I do not know! Am I my brother’s keeper?

chapters.title: Genesis 5: The Generations of Adam
chapters.subtitle: The Genealogy of the Patriarchs and Enoch Who Walked with God
chapters.synopsis: The sacred record of ten generations from Adam through Seth down to Noah. Enoch walks faithfully with God and is taken without seeing death. The chapter culminates in Lamech naming his son Noah: 'He will comfort us.'

panels.altText: Enoch ascending peacefully along a glowing stairway of starlight into the celestial heights

bubbles.text: Altogether, Enoch lived a total of 365 years. Enoch walked faithfully with God; then he was no more, because God took him away.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 5:21–24

panels.altText: Patriarch holding the newborn infant Noah against the backdrop of ancient timber forests

bubbles.text: Lamech fathered a son and named him Noah, saying, 'He will comfort us in the labor and painful toil of our hands caused by the ground the Lord has cursed.'
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 5:28–32

bubbles.text: He will bring us rest and comfort from our painful toil.
bubbles.speaker: Lamech

chapters.title: Genesis 6: The Ark of Noah
chapters.subtitle: Human Wickedness and The Heavenly Blueprint
chapters.synopsis: Grief grips the Lord as corruption and violence spread across the earth. But Noah finds favor in His eyes. God commands Noah to build a massive wooden ark of gopher wood to preserve life from the coming flood.

panels.altText: Noah standing in contemplative prayer on a hillside as dark storm clouds gather on the horizon

bubbles.text: The Lord saw how great the wickedness of the human race had become. But Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, and he walked faithfully with God.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 6:5–8

panels.altText: The colossal wooden ribs of Noah's Ark rising against the forest hills under purposeful construction

bubbles.text: God said to Noah: 'Make yourself an ark of cypress wood; coat it with pitch inside and out. I will establish my covenant with you, and you will enter the ark—you and your family and pairs of every living thing.'

bubbles.speaker: The Lord

chapters.title: Genesis 7: The Great Deluge
chapters.subtitle: The Fountains of the Deep Burst and Rain Floods the Earth
chapters.synopsis: Noah, his family, and the creatures enter the Ark. The Lord shuts the door behind them. The springs of the great deep burst forth and the floodgates of heaven pour down rain for forty days and forty nights.

panels.altText: Pairs of animals boarding the great ramp of the Ark as the heavy timber door seals shut

bubbles.text: Pairs of all creatures that have the breath of life came to Noah and entered the ark. Then the Lord shut him in.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 7:1–16

panels.altText: The Ark riding majestically atop churning ocean waves beneath torrential rain and lightning

bubbles.text: For forty days the flood kept coming on the earth. The waters rose and lifted the ark high above the earth; all the high mountains under the entire heavens were covered.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 7:17–24

chapters.title: Genesis 8: The Waters Recede
chapters.subtitle: The Raven, The Dove with the Olive Leaf, and The Altar
chapters.synopsis: God remembers Noah. The wind blows, the floodgates close, and the Ark rests on the mountains of Ararat. Noah sends forth a raven and a dove, which returns with an olive branch. Noah builds an altar of thanksgiving.

panels.altText: A white dove with a green olive leaf flying toward Noah's hand at the Ark's window as sun rays pierce clouds

bubbles.text: When the dove returned to him in the evening, there in its beak was a freshly plucked olive leaf! Then Noah knew that the water had receded from the earth.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 8:6–12

panels.altText: Noah and his family standing in reverence by a stone altar atop Mount Ararat as the waters gleam below

bubbles.text: Noah built an altar to the Lord and sacrificed burnt offerings on it. The Lord smelled the pleasing aroma and said in His heart: 'Never again will I curse the ground because of humans.'

bubbles.text: As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will never cease.

chapters.title: Genesis 9: The Rainbow Covenant
chapters.subtitle: God's Everlasting Promise to Every Living Creature
chapters.synopsis: God blesses Noah and his sons. He establishes the rainbow in the clouds as the sign of His everlasting covenant never again to destroy all flesh by water.

panels.altText: A luminous, vibrant double rainbow spanning across a golden post-flood mountain valley

bubbles.text: God said: 'I have set my rainbow in the clouds, and it will be the sign of the covenant between me and the earth... whenever the rainbow appears, I will remember my everlasting promise.'

bubbles.text: I set my rainbow in the clouds, and it will be the sign of the covenant.

chapters.subtitle: The Descendants of Shem, Ham, and Japheth
chapters.synopsis: The genealogy of the seventy nations arising from the three sons of Noah, spreading across maritime coastlands, ancient Mesopotamia, Canaan, and the fertile crescent.

panels.altText: An ancient parchment map showing sea routes and migrations across the Mediterranean and Euphrates

bubbles.text: These are the clans of Noah's sons, according to their lines of descent, within their nations. From these the nations spread out over the earth after the flood.

chapters.title: Genesis 11: The Tower of Babel
chapters.subtitle: Human Ambition and The Confusion of Tongues
chapters.synopsis: The whole world had one language. Men gather on the plain of Shinar to build a tower reaching to the heavens to make a name for themselves. The Lord confuses their speech and scatters them over the earth.

panels.altText: The monumental spiraling ziggurat tower rising into the clouds amidst bustling workers and kilns

bubbles.text: They said to each other, 'Come, let’s make bricks and bake them thoroughly.' Then they said, 'Come, let us build ourselves a city, with a tower that reaches to the heavens, so that we may make a name for ourselves.'
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 11:1–4
Builders of Babel
bubbles.text: Come! Let us build a city with a tower reaching to the heavens!

panels.altText: Scattered caravans and peoples departing in different directions away from the unfinished tower at sunset

chapters.subtitle: A New Name: Israel – Striving with God and Prevailing

chapters.synopsis: Jacob loves seventeen-year-old Joseph more than all his sons and gives him an ornate multi-colored coat. Joseph dreams of sheaves and stars bowing to him, stoking his brothers' hatred. When sent to Dothan, they throw him into a pit and sell him to Ishmaelite traders.

chapters.subtitle: Unfaithfulness, Righteousness, and The Messianic Line

chapters.title: Genesis 45: Joseph Reveals Himself
chapters.subtitle: I Am Joseph! God Sent Me Ahead to Save Lives
chapters.synopsis: Joseph can no longer control himself. He orders all Egyptians to leave, weeps loudly, and reveals: 'I am Joseph! Is my father still living?' He comforts his terrified brothers, explaining that God orchestrated events to preserve a remnant. Pharaoh invites Jacob's family to settle in Goshen.

panels.altText: Joseph weeping openly with tears streaming down his face, reaching out both arms to his stunned brothers

bubbles.text: Joseph wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard him. He said to his brothers: 'I am Joseph! Does my father still live?' He said: 'Do not be distressed or angry with yourselves for selling me here, because it was to save lives that God sent me ahead of you.'

chapters.title: Genesis 46: Jacob Goes to Egypt
chapters.subtitle: Do Not Be Afraid to Go Down to Egypt
chapters.synopsis: Israel sets out for Egypt. At Beersheba, God speaks in visions of the night: 'Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.' Israel and his seventy descendants travel in Pharaoh's wagons to Goshen, where Joseph rushes to embrace his father.

chapters.title: Genesis 47: The Land of Goshen and Famine Wisdom
chapters.subtitle: Jacob Blesses Pharaoh and Sells Grain in Famine
chapters.synopsis: Joseph presents his father and brothers to Pharaoh. Jacob blesses the mighty ruler of Egypt. The family settles in the fertile land of Rameses/Goshen. As the famine worsens, Joseph wisely manages the grain supply, saving Egypt from starvation.

bubbles.text: Joseph brought his father Jacob in and presented him before Pharaoh. Jacob blessed Pharaoh. Pharaoh asked him, 'How old are you?' Jacob answered, 'The years of my pilgrimage are a hundred and thirty.'

chapters.title: Genesis 48: Jacob Blesses Joseph's Sons
chapters.subtitle: The Crossing of Hands: Ephraim and Manasseh
chapters.synopsis: Jacob falls ill. Joseph brings his two sons Manasseh and Ephraim. Though nearly blind, Jacob intentionally crosses his hands, placing his right hand upon the younger Ephraim and his left upon the firstborn Manasseh, blessing them with the covenant of Abraham.

chapters.title: Genesis 49: Jacob's Prophetic Blessing
chapters.subtitle: The Scepter of Judah and The Twelve Tribes of Israel
chapters.synopsis: Jacob gathers his twelve sons around his deathbed and delivers prophetic blessings concerning the destiny of the twelve tribes. He prophesies the royal scepter and Shiloh from Judah, and the fruitful bough of Joseph. He charges them to bury him in the Cave of Machpelah.

panels.altText: The silhouette of a majestic royal lion of Judah standing proudly beneath a blazing sunset horizon

bubbles.text: Jacob prophesied over Judah: 'Judah, your brothers will praise you... You are a lion’s cub, Judah. The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet, until he to whom it belongs shall come.'
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 49:8–10

bubbles.text: The scepter will not depart from Judah... until He comes to whom it belongs; the obedience of the nations shall be His.
bubbles.speaker: Jacob

bubbles.text: When Jacob had finished giving instructions to his sons, he drew his feet up into the bed, breathed his last and was gathered to his people.

chapters.title: Genesis 50: Forgiveness and Legacy
chapters.subtitle: God Meant It for Good: The Conclusion of Genesis
chapters.synopsis: Jacob is embalmed and carried with a great Egyptian and Hebrew procession to Canaan, buried in the Cave of Machpelah. The brothers fear Joseph will now take revenge. Joseph weeps and speaks comfort: 'You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good.' Joseph dies full of faith, instructing his bones to be carried up to the Promised Land.

panels.altText: A grand, dignified funeral procession of chariots and riders winding through the hills of Canaan toward Machpelah

bubbles.text: Joseph threw himself on his father and wept over him and kissed him. A great cortege of Egyptian chariots, horsemen, and all the house of Israel accompanied Jacob’s body to the Cave of Machpelah in Canaan.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 50:1–14

panels.altText: Joseph gently lifting his kneeling brothers with eyes full of tears and forgiveness under warm palace arches

bubbles.text: Joseph's brothers came and threw themselves down before him. But Joseph said to them: 'Don’t be afraid. Am I in the place of God? You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good to accomplish what is now being done, the saving of many lives.' And he spoke kindly to them and comforted them.
bubbles.speaker: Genesis 50:15–21
